method: Built-in image_gen generation followed by a targeted image_gen edit; WebP format conversion only.
role: Schematic illustration of a cellular torus, a face boundary, and an essential cycle; exact maps are defined in the accompanying note.
initial_prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a beautiful, restrained three-dimensional mathematical concept illustration for a mathematical physicist's academic website about algebraic topology and error correction. Landscape aspect ratio 3:2, warm ivory museum-paper background with ample clean negative space. ONE central exquisitely rendered torus surface seen in elevated three-quarter view, its central hole clearly visible; matte translucent blue-grey ceramic/glass, a very fine coherent quadrilateral cellular mesh following both periodic directions. On a small near-front region highlight ONE square face in translucent teal with a thin deep-teal closed four-edge boundary, gently thickened and clearly a small contractible cell boundary. Mark this small face with the italic symbol f and the nearby loop with z_b = ∂₂f. On the SAME torus show ONE distinct beautiful muted-gold closed loop tracing the torus longitude around its central hole, through the cellular mesh, a cycle that cannot be the boundary of a collection of faces. Mark the gold loop z_ℓ. Keep the two loops visually separated. A few restrained navy dots at relevant cell vertices are acceptable. At the lower right on the paper, small elegant scholarly math only: H₁(T²; 𝔽₂) ≅ 𝔽₂². No other text, no title, no explanatory prose. The picture must communicate boundaries versus nontrivial cycles, with subtle topological shape, precise mesh, polished materials and soft contact shadows. Orthographic scientific-render aesthetics, physically restrained teal/navy/gold palette, no cosmic background, no stars, no neon glow, no extraneous symbols, no qubits or circuitry, no infographic boxes or busy collage. Ensure the noncontractible gold line is truly one closed loop and the tiny teal face boundary is a separate closed loop. Elegant, intellectually inviting, not a marketing poster.
final_edit_prompt: Refine this precise mathematical illustration with ONE targeted correction: the teal contractible face f currently shares its bottom edge with the gold noncontractible loop. Move the entire teal face highlight DOWN by one complete mesh row into a quadrilateral cell on the LOWER FRONT wall of the torus, fully BELOW the gold loop, so the teal closed four-edge face boundary and the gold loop share NO edges or vertices and are visibly separated by at least one row of grey mesh. Place the face at the lower-front center-left, with its four complete deep-teal boundary edges, its f label, and nearby z_b = ∂₂f annotation moved with it and not overlapping gold. Restore the old face location to the normal blue-grey torus mesh. Preserve the elegant torus, all other mesh lines, the single gold noncontractible loop, z_ℓ label, lower-right H₁(T²;𝔽₂) ≅ 𝔽₂² annotation, ivory background, colors, materials, composition and shading. No new text or objects. Ensure the small teal boundary is a closed four-edge cycle around exactly one quadrilateral mesh cell well below the gold line.
